facts: Henry Thomson authored the paper 'Authoritarian Repression and Electoral Opposition: Mobilization under Germany's Antisocialist Law'.
The paper was published in Comparative Politics on 2022-07-01 (DOI: 10.5129/001041522x16346476699950).
The study examines the effect of targeted repression of opposition party leaders on mobilization under electoral authoritarianism.
The historical case analyzed is Imperial Germany from 1878 to 1890, when the social democratic party was banned and its leaders were expelled from home districts.
Methodologically, the author estimates difference-in-differences models exploiting variation in the timing and frequency of leader expulsions across electoral districts.
The analysis finds that expulsions caused declines in social democrats' electoral support directly and indirectly through activist and voter support.
The negative electoral effects of expulsions diminished with each additional expulsion and after the first election post-expulsions.
Local party organizations and ideological leadership adapted over time to mitigate the effects of repression and maintain mobilization.
